config.gitstudio.ai.anthropicModelDeep.d: Anthropic model ID for opt-in deep reasoning.
config.gitstudio.ai.anthropicModelFast.d: Anthropic model ID for fast/cheap tasks (commit messages).
config.gitstudio.ai.anthropicModelMid.de: Anthropic model ID for mid-tier tasks (explain diff, summaries).
config.gitstudio.ai.cliAgent.description: The local agent CLI to drive (uses its own login, no API key). Set via the GitStudio · AI panel; used when the provider is a local agent.
config.gitstudio.ai.cliModel.description: Optional model override passed to the local agent CLI (blank = the CLI's default).
config.gitstudio.ai.commitStyle.descript: How AI-generated commit messages are styled.
config.gitstudio.ai.commitStyle.enumDesc: A single concise subject line, no body.
Imperative subject plus a short explanatory body.
config.gitstudio.ai.openai.baseUrl.markd: Base URL for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/chat/completions` is appended). Examples: `https://api.openai.com/v1` (OpenAI), `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` (OpenRouter), `http://localhost:11434/v1` (Ollama), `http://localhost:1234/v1` (LM Studio).
config.gitstudio.ai.openai.modelDeep.des: OpenAI-compatible model ID for opt-in deep reasoning.
config.gitstudio.ai.openai.modelFast.des: OpenAI-compatible model ID for fast/cheap tasks (commit messages). For a local server use its model name, e.g. llama3.1 or qwen2.5-coder.
config.gitstudio.ai.openai.modelMid.desc: OpenAI-compatible model ID for mid-tier tasks (explain diff, summaries).
config.gitstudio.ai.provider.enumDescrip: Prefer the zero-key VS Code Language Model (GitHub Copilot / Cursor) when available; otherwise Anthropic (if a key is set), then an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (if a model is configured).
Use the VS Code Language Model API — GitHub Copilot or Cursor's models, with no key. Pick a specific model via “GitStudio: Select AI Model…”.
Use Anthropic directly (requires an API key, set with “GitStudio: Connect AI Provider”).
Use any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — OpenAI, Codex, OpenRouter, or a local server (Ollama / LM Studio). Configure the base URL and model below; a key is optional for local servers.
Use a local agent CLI — Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI — with its own login and no API key. Which one is gitstudio.ai.cliAgent; pick it with “GitStudio: Connect AI Provider”.
config.gitstudio.ai.provider.markdownDes: Which provider GitStudio uses for its optional AI features. AI is off until a provider is available; it never gates or breaks Git operations. Use **GitStudio: Select AI Model…** for a guided picker.
config.gitstudio.ai.reviewPrompt.markdow: Custom system prompt for **Review Changes (AI)**. Leave empty to use GitStudio's built-in code-review prompt. Set your own to steer the review (e.g. focus areas, house style, output format).
config.gitstudio.ai.title: AI
config.gitstudio.avatars.gravatar.markdo: Show commit authors' pictures in the Commit Graph, the Commits view and commit details. To find one, GitStudio sends an MD5 hash of each author's email address to Gravatar (`www.gravatar.com`, run by Automattic); for a GitHub noreply address (`…@users.noreply.github.com`) it asks GitHub (`avatars.githubusercontent.com`) for that account's picture instead. Turn this off to show every author as coloured initials and send neither request. While you are signed in to GitHub, the pictures GitHub itself returns (on pull requests, and for the authors of a GitHub repository's recent commits) still show. See [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/GitStudioHQ/gitstudio/blob/main/apps/extension/PRIVACY.md).
While blame annotations are shown, clicking one reveals that commit in the GitStudio Commit Graph, opened beside the code.
config.gitstudio.blame.gutter.colors.des: Background tint for the blame annotation gutter.
config.gitstudio.blame.gutter.colors.enu: Tint by commit age — a code-age heatmap (recent warmer, older cooler).
Give every author their own stable tint.
config.gitstudio.blame.gutter.fields.des: Which columns the blame annotation gutter shows. Configure them from the annotation right-click menu: Git Blame Annotations → Options.
How author names are written in the blame annotation gutter.
config.gitstudio.blame.heatmap.descripti: Tint full-file blame annotations with a code-age heatmap (recent changes warmer, older changes cooler).
config.gitstudio.blame.inlineEnabled.des: Show inline blame for the current line (author, relative time, and summary) at the end of the line.
config.gitstudio.blame.showDiffOnHover.d: Show the commit behind a line — message, author, date, and a copyable SHA — when hovering it.
Show the current line's commit author and age in the status bar.
config.gitstudio.blame.title: Blame
config.gitstudio.changes.autoRefresh.des: Keep the Changes list up to date on its own — after you save a file, and when the window regains focus so edits made by other tools show up too. Turn this off on a very large repository to refresh only on demand.
config.gitstudio.changes.stagingModel.de: How the Changes view presents your work. Either way, committing with nothing ticked or staged offers to commit everything after asking.
config.gitstudio.changes.stagingModel.en: Separate Staged and Unstaged groups — the clearest view of what is going into this commit.
One list with a tick per file, JetBrains-style. Ticking a file stages it, so both models are the same underlying Git state.
config.gitstudio.changes.title: Changes & Staging
config.gitstudio.changesBadge.descriptio: Show a count badge on the GitStudio activity-bar icon for changed files in the working tree (like the built-in Source Control badge). The tooltip also reports commits waiting to be pulled.
config.gitstudio.commit.signoffByDefault: Enable the Sign-off toggle by default in the GitStudio commit box (adds a Signed-off-by trailer).
config.gitstudio.commit.title: Commit & Sync
config.gitstudio.debug.logChildProcesses: Log every child process GitStudio launches - the binary, its full arguments, the working directory, and the environment variables GitStudio adds - to the GitStudio: Process Audit output channel. Turn this on only while reproducing a problem you want to report: it is how an OS-level prompt raised by a child process (a credential helper, a git hook, an editor binary) is traced back to the exact command that caused it. Secret-looking values are scrubbed.
Send **anonymous, scrubbed crash reports** when a GitStudio command fails, so we can find and fix bugs during the beta without waiting for someone to file a report. Only the shape of a failure is sent (error type/message/stack or the failed operation), tagged with a random install id and your OS/editor version, and it is scrubbed first: paths, file and branch names, commit subjects, emails, tokens and remote repository names are taken out wherever the scrubber recognises them (a remote's host name, such as github.com, is kept). See [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/GitStudioHQ/gitstudio/blob/main/apps/extension/PRIVACY.md). Reports are also gated by VS Code's global `telemetry.telemetryLevel`: set that to `off` to disable regardless of this toggle. Turn this off to opt out entirely.
config.gitstudio.errorReporting.endpoint: Collector URL that anonymous crash reports are POSTed to as a plain JSON body. Defaults to GitStudio's collector; point it at any endpoint you control, or **leave it blank to disable sending entirely**. If unreachable, reporting silently no-ops.
config.gitstudio.fetch.prune.description: Pass --prune when fetching, so remote-tracking branches deleted on the remote disappear from the branch list instead of lingering as stale entries. Never touches local branches.
config.gitstudio.general.title: General
config.gitstudio.merge.autoApplyNonConfl: Open the merge editor with every non-conflicting change already applied (JetBrains' "apply non-conflicting changes" on open). Off: they wait for you, one click each or all at once from the toolbar.
config.gitstudio.merge.autoOpen.markdown: When a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, git am or stash pop stops on conflicts: show the **Conflicts** dashboard, open a conflicted file in the GitStudio merge editor as soon as you switch to it, and take over VS Code's built-in merge editor tab. Off: nothing opens by itself — use **GitStudio: Resolve Conflicts…**. (This used to open every conflicted file as its own tab.) If Merge Studio is also installed, it leaves this to GitStudio; turn this off to let Merge Studio open conflicts instead.
config.gitstudio.merge.title: Merge & Diff
config.gitstudio.pr.defaultMergeMethod.d: Default method offered first when merging a pull request.
config.gitstudio.pr.defaultMergeMethod.e: Squash the PR's commits into one and merge.
Rebase the PR's commits onto the base and merge.
config.gitstudio.staging.clickGutterTogg: Stage or unstage a change by clicking the gutter beside it. Off by default: VS Code gives decorations no click event, so this is inferred from a click landing at the start of a line — which is also how you place a caret. It never fires on a line without a change, and yields while blame annotations are shown.
config.gitstudio.staging.showGutterState: Show which changes are staged in the editor gutter. The glyph reports state only — VS Code's API does not allow an extension to make a gutter icon clickable. Toggle a change with the keybinding, by right-clicking its line number, or on GitStudio's own diff page.
config.gitstudio.statusBar.showGraph.des: Show a status-bar button that opens the Commit Graph.
Show a status-bar button that opens a terminal already in the active repository's root — which is not necessarily the workspace root.
config.gitstudio.worktrees.prefixWithPro: No longer used: New Worktree now suggests the folder '<project>-<branch>' beside the main worktree, and you can edit it before it is created.
description: Free, open-source Git GUI & commit graph for VS Code and Cursor. Git Studio brings a JetBrains-style Git workflow into the editor — inline blame, file history, hunk & line staging, 3-pane merge, interactive rebase with universal Undo, stash/shelf, worktrees, and in-editor GitHub PRs. A free alternative to GitLens, GitKraken & Sourcetree.

walkthrough.gitstudio.gettingStarted.des: A free, JetBrains-grade Git suite — commit graph, blame, history, hunk staging, 3-pane merge, interactive rebase with Undo, and optional BYO-key AI. Take the tour.
walkthrough.gitstudio.gettingStarted.git: A commit opened from a blamed line: its author, message, the branches it is on and the file it changed, beside the graph

Who last changed the line you are on, and when — at the end of the line and in the status bar. **Annotate with Git Blame** adds a column beside every line, tinted by age; click an annotation and its commit opens in the graph, with its message, its author and the files it changed.
[Annotate with Git Blame](command:gitstudio.toggleFileBlame)
Shortcut: __Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+G B__ in any editor.
See who changed a line, and why
The AI settings: the editor's own AI connected and ready, and the other ways to connect a model

Sign in once with VS Code's built-in GitHub account to list, check out, review, merge, and create pull requests in-editor. AI is optional: it uses Copilot's (or Cursor's) model when there is one, with nothing to set up; otherwise connect Anthropic, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or a local agent CLI for commit messages, explain-this-diff, and summaries. It never gates a Git operation, and Disable AI Features turns it off.
[Sign in to GitHub](command:gitstudio.pr.signIn)
[Connect AI Provider](command:gitstudio.ai.connect)
GitStudio is free and open source. [Support GitStudio…](command:gitstudio.support)
The Commit Graph: branch lanes, branch and tag chips, and the authors of the commits on main, a feature branch and a release branch

Your history as a commit graph: colored lanes for branches, chips for branches and tags, and who wrote each commit. It is in the **Commits** view, under Changes in the GitStudio sidebar, and in the **Commit Graph** panel beside the terminal. Right-click a commit to check it out, cherry-pick it, branch from it or reset to it; select two to compare them.
[Show Commit Graph](command:gitstudio.showCommitGraph)
Browse your history in the commit graph
Line History for two lines of a file: the three commits that changed them, with their authors and ages

Every commit that changed the lines you select, newest first — pick one to see its diff. Step a whole file back and forth through its revisions, and find lost work in the reflog.
[Show Line History](command:gitstudio.showLineHistory)
Shortcut: __Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+G H__ on the current line.
The three-pane merge editor stopped on a conflict: changes from main, the result, and changes from feature

When a merge, rebase or cherry-pick stops on a conflict, GitStudio opens a three-pane editor — your side, the result and theirs — where an arrow takes a change into the result. Interactive rebase gets the same care.
[Start Interactive Rebase…](command:gitstudio.startInteractiveRebase)
Made a mistake? __Undo Last Git Operation__ (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+G Z) reverses it.
The Changes view with ticks: one file's changes open, one of them ticked, and a commit message ready

Stage whole files, or tick single changes inside one, in the **Changes** view, then commit from its commit box (Amend, Sign-off, a different author, Commit & Push). With AI on, the sparkle button in the box drafts a message from what you staged. Your stashes are listed under your changes: open one to see every file it holds, and **Move to Changes** just the files you want back.
[Open the Changes view](command:workbench.view.extension.gitstudio)
In the editor: select lines and press __Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+G S__ to stage the changes they touch.
